solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Returning sick of Mexican food

indicators.note: returning means the word for sick is read backwards, coming back the way it went

parts.note: to cat is British slang for to vomit, so sick gives cat
o' is the clipped form of of, as in man o' war

explanation.surface: Someone coming home thoroughly fed up with eating Mexican dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick of' looks like one phrase meaning fed up, but the two words work separately. 'Returning' turns only the slang word for vomit, giving TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla with a filling is a classic dish of Mexico, so it is an example of that cuisine.

clue.text: Traffic delays follow vehicle overturning near Kansas

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning means the word for vehicle is written upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle for hire
KS is the US postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Delays on the road caused by a vehicle overturning on a Kansas highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Queues of stopped vehicles stretching back along a road are what drivers know as delays in traffic.

clue.text: Once more flying over centre of Austria, out of touch

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the next one

parts.note: flying again means travelling in a further aircraft, that is on another plane

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the seven-letter word Austria

explanation.surface: Someone taking yet another flight over the heart of Austria, losing contact.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of AUSTRIA is T, placed below the phrase for flying again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to be living in another world is idiomatically detached from reality, so out of touch.

clue.text: Flying Dutchman perhaps and German leader smuggled drug to artist

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of German

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran
dope is slang for a drug
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A German boss caught smuggling narcotics to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying Dutchman' looks like a ghost ship or a person, but it is Wagner's opera, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Der fliegende Holländer is an example of large-scale, fully sung serious opera.

clue.text: Made special appearance and blustered, taking in English

indicators.note: taking in means the word for blustered holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: wind that blustered blew in gusts, so it gusted

explanation.surface: A guest star who made a cameo and ranted, roping in an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To guest is to appear as a visiting performer on someone else's show, a special appearance.

clue.text: Head of Academy established American composer in film

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of Academy

parts.note: to made something is to have established it, as in made a name
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An academy's principal set up an American composer's biopic.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Shaffer's play and Milos Forman's film about Mozart take his middle name as their title.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1984 film about Mozart is titled with his middle name, so it is the composer in a film.

clue.text: Dee — river producing very slow flow

parts.note: Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: The River Dee yielding only a trickle of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' looks like the river, but it is the letter D spelt out; the Ribble is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle of liquid that barely moves is described as a slow, thin flow of drops.

clue.text: They fool about sporting lacier jockstrap

indicators.note: sporting suggests frolicking or playing about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jokers prancing around in a rather lacy athletic support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as wearing, but it signals rearranging LACIER JOCKSTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pranksters who play tricks on people are those who fool about for laughs.

clue.text: Tree covering more than half of Channel Island

indicators.note: more than half of keeps five of the eight letters of the island name, dropping the tail

parts.note: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands between England and France

explanation.surface: Trees blanketing much of one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Where film is not exposed

parts.note: photographic film stays unexposed inside the device that holds it; the legal phrase also means in private, away from public view

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in private chambers, and literally film sits unseen inside the device.

clue.text: I am like Father William perhaps seen through the looking-glass

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
in Lewis Carroll's poem 'You are old, Father William', the man is aged

explanation.surface: A Carroll reader identifies with an old character seen in the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: Father William comes from Alice in Wonderland; the looking-glass nods to Carroll's other book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen in a mirror has been reflected, so it has been imaged or pictured.

clue.text: Withdraw making cry of pain in fight

indicators.note: in means the cry is placed inside the word for fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight, especially a boxing match
ow is what one cries when hurt

explanation.surface: A boxer quitting after yelping during the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow out is an idiom for retiring or stepping back from something, so withdrawing.

clue.text: Cause to resent bit of bile in one throwing out

indicators.note: in means the small piece goes inside the word for something throwing out

parts.note: an emitter is something that gives out or throws out radiation or light

indicators.note: bit of takes just the first letter of bile

explanation.surface: A little bile in someone who vomits makes them sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone bitter is to make them feel resentment, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spaces in electronic manuscript

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: Gaps between words in a digital manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing an em is a unit of space, so these are typographical spaces.

clue.text: Pieces of leather concealed in yachting centre

indicators.note: in means the word for concealed goes inside the place name

parts.note: Cowes on the Isle of Wight is the home of British yachting and Cowes Week
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Leather goods hidden away in a sailing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned cattle skins are pieces of leather.

clue.text: Cut tax

definitions.meaning: a duty levied on goods made at home

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means remove by cutting, and the noun is a duty charged on home-produced goods.

clue.text: Curses late unreliable cars touring Spain

indicators.note: touring means the pieces go round the next letter, holding it inside

parts.note: ex means former, so late as in the late president
crates is slang for old, rickety cars
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone swearing at rattletrap hire cars on a late tour of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or curse someone bitterly.

clue.text: Strong drinks right in small measures

indicators.note: in means the letter for right goes inside the word for small measures

parts.note: shots are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: Spirits served in small tots, quite rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs a short is a small measure of spirits, as opposed to a long drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts in British usage are spirits such as whisky served in small measures, so strong drinks.

clue.text: Screaming colour

definitions.meaning: an outcry, as in the phrase ... and cry, a loud public clamour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a shade of colour and also an outcry, as in hue and cry, so screaming.

clue.text: Mac's accessory to wear mostly keeping one out of rain

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for wear is dropped

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them

indicators.note: keeping with out of means holding a letter outside the word rain
out of joins keeping to say the letter is removed from rain

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's waterproof accessory, worn mostly to keep out the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' suggests a raincoat, but it is a Scotsman; the sporran is the pouch worn with a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a kilt, a Scotsman's accessory.

clue.text: Record systematically time a vehicle mostly departed

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the vehicle is dropped

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: Logging the times of buses, most of which had already left.
explanation.definitionFit: To tabulate is to arrange data in a table, recording it systematically.

clue.text: Sweet, made up in plaits

indicators.note: in a down clue made up means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding or dessert course

explanation.surface: A pudding concocted in braided form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like an anagram signal or invention, but in a down clue it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair worn in tresses, long locks or plaits, is described as tressed.

clue.text: Instrument gives start of ballad equally well

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of ballad

parts.note: as soon, as in I'd as soon stay, means equally willingly

explanation.surface: A woodwind instrument opening a song just as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a low-pitched double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Expression of praise that's not rare

definitions.meaning: a congratulation said after a success
steak cooked through, the opposite of rare

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase congratulates someone, and also describes steak cooked thoroughly rather than rare.

clue.text: One spelling 'Transposition', disregarding 'S'

indicators.note: disregarding means the named letter is ignored, so taken away

parts.note: a switch is an exchange or transposition

explanation.surface: Someone spelling out a word puzzle, ignoring the letter S.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spelling' reads as someone spelling words, but means one who casts spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts spells, so she is one doing spelling in the magical sense.

clue.text: One exhibiting uninspiring lot

definitions.meaning: someone who shows things, a displayer
British slang for a useless, disappointing group of people

explanation.definitionFit: Read as show plus er it is a person who displays; British slang uses it for a useless bunch.

clue.text: Note sound of man's voice

indicators.note: sound of means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the tenor is the high adult male singing voice

explanation.surface: A musical note sounding like a man's high voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music, but it is a banknote: a TENNER is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound banknote is called a tenner in Britain, so it is a note.

clue.text: Defect in bicycle wheel perhaps made discordant noises

definitions.meaning: a wire rod of a wheel that has come loose and sticks out

explanation.definitionFit: A displaced wheel rod is a fault in a wheel, and to protest openly is to voice dissent.

clue.text: Tracking down Mafia boss in East Anglian town

parts.note: hunting is tracking down quarry
a don is a Mafia chief

explanation.surface: A gangster chief being pursued in a provincial English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, part of the East Anglia region of England.

clue.text: Without places to recuperate

definitions.meaning: the French loan word for lacking
short for sanatoriums, places where invalids recover

explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means lacking, and the plural of the abbreviation san means sanatoriums.
